primary.title: De revolutionibus orbium coelestium
primary.author: Nicolaus Copernicus
primary.rationale: Copernicus's seminal work, presenting his heliocentric model of the universe. This is the most important primary source for understanding his scientific contributions.

primary.title: Commentariolus
primary.author: Nicolaus Copernicus
primary.rationale: An earlier, shorter manuscript outlining the basic principles of his heliocentric theory, circulated among friends before the publication of 'De revolutionibus'.

primary.title: De lateribus et angulis triangulorum
primary.author: Nicolaus Copernicus
primary.rationale: Copernicus's work on trigonometry, demonstrating his mathematical expertise and its application to astronomical problems.

secondary.title: The Cambridge Companion to Copernicus
secondary.author: Nick Jardine
secondary.rationale: A collection of essays by leading scholars covering various aspects of Copernicus's life, work, and legacy, offering comprehensive scholarly analysis.

secondary.title: Copernicus: An Intellectual Biography
secondary.author: Edward Rosen
secondary.rationale: A foundational biography that provides in-depth analysis of Copernicus's intellectual development and the context of his scientific revolution.

secondary.title: Nicolaus Copernicus: Reason, Religion, and the Revolution of the Heavenly Spheres
secondary.author: Owen Gingerich
secondary.rationale: A highly regarded scholarly biography by a renowned historian of science, offering a detailed and nuanced perspective on Copernicus's life and work.

suggestions.notes: Primary sources are likely to be found in digitized manuscript collections or early printed book archives on Internet Archive. Modern scholarly editions and translations may also be available.
